title: Robot routes across a warehouse
prompt:
A robot starts in the top-left cell of a warehouse floor plan and must reach the bottom-right cell. It can only move one cell right or one cell down at a time. A cell holding 1 is shelving and cannot be entered; 0 is open floor. Return how many different routes the robot can take, modulo 1,000,000,007. If the start or the finish is shelving, the answer is 0.

- grid has 1 to 100 rows and 1 to 100 columns; every row has the same length.
- Each cell is 0 or 1.
hints: Every route into a cell arrives from the cell above or the cell to its left, and those two sets of routes never overlap.
So routes(r, c) = routes(r − 1, c) + routes(r, c − 1) for an open cell, and 0 for shelving.
Fill row by row. One array of length cols is enough: before the update ways[c] still holds the row above, and ways[c − 1] already holds this row.

solution.explanation: This is grid DP. The number of routes into an open cell is the sum of the routes into the cell above and the cell to its left, because the last move is either down or right. Shelving cells hold 0. Rows are filled top to bottom, left to right, so both inputs are ready when a cell is computed. A single row array is reused: ways[c] still holds the value from the row above until it is overwritten.

complexity.notes: Each cell is visited once with constant work. Keeping one row instead of the full table cuts the space from O(R × C) to O(C).

followUps: Return one route as a string of R and D moves instead of the count.
The robot may also move diagonally down-right. What changes?
